collections.label: Assets
collections.description: Devices. Status (identified, verified, trusted…) is derived by Powerfarm from jobs and evidence and cannot be edited.

collections.label: Recovery operations
collections.description: One proposed operation on one device. Publishing it is the approval.

collections.label: Events
collections.description: Searchable copy of the operational journal. Written only by Powerfarm.

collections.label: Evidence
collections.description: Append-only. Files are hashed by the server.

collections.label: Releases
collections.description: A release is drafted by CI and approved by publishing: by someone holding release.production who is not its author. Only an approved release can be deployed.

collections.label: Clients
collections.description: Organisations and people Powerfarm serves. Register in Powerfarm → Register; publishing is approval. Activation needs its controls met.

collections.label: Services
collections.description: The canonical service catalogue. Register a service once; projects, products and contracts reference it. Deployments are service instances.

fields.label: Merged into (code of the surviving record)

collections.label: Service instances
collections.description: One concrete deployment of a catalogue service. Credentials are never stored here: record where they live in Secret references.

fields.label: Merged into (code of the surviving record)

collections.label: Contracts
collections.description: Agreement records. Confidential by default. Signing is a person's attestation with the signed copy attached; nothing signs automatically.

fields.label: Merged into (code of the surviving record)

collections.label: Blueprints
collections.description: Onboarding templates. Publishing (administrators only) activates that exact revision. Steps use a fixed action catalogue; nothing executes code.

collections.label: Work items
collections.description: Tasks, approvals and link requests. Approvals are resolved in Powerfarm → Automation by a person with the required role.

fields.label: Decision (approvals: approve / reject; needs attention: retry / done_by_hand / give_up)

collections.label: Identifiers
collections.description: The identity registry: one entry per identifier, unique across every record type. Maintained by Powerfarm from each record's Identifiers field; administrators transfer one by changing its subject, with a rationale.

collections.label: Incidents
collections.description: What Powerfarm vigilance found on a managed device, or a refused device message. Opened by Powerfarm; people investigate and resolve them here.

collections.label: Device profiles
collections.description: Configuration profiles for managed devices. Publishing by an administrator approves one: required profiles are then installed by Powerfarm MDM on every matching device; any profile on a device that is not listed here is reported as an incident.

collections.label: Security exceptions
collections.description: A time-limited, approved waiver of one control on one entity. Publishing by an administrator is the risk acceptance.

collections.label: People
collections.description: One canonical record per person. Lifecycle: intake = invited, active, suspended, retired = departed. Sign-in identities (EmDash user, OIDC subject, Managed Apple Account, Git) are Identifiers; e-mail and phone are contact details only.

Access groups (coarse, sent to Cloudflare Access)

collections.label: Organisations
collections.description: Powerfarm itself (OR-0001) and the organisations it deals with as institutions. Holds legal identity and the institutional accounts that must never depend on one person.

fields.label: Merged into (code of the surviving record)
Institutional accounts (Cloudflare, Apple Business Manager, MDM push owner, developer team, repositories)

collections.label: Agents
collections.description: Non-human principals: AI agents, CI runners and release services, each a separate identity with a responsible person. Never signs in with a human method.

fields.label: Merged into (code of the surviving record)

collections.label: Grants
collections.description: Explicit authority. Publishing a grant (by someone holding authority.grant, never to themselves) makes it effective; unpublishing or expiry revokes it.

collections.label: Policies
collections.description: Versioned institutional rules. Each published revision is sealed. A policy is 'enforced' only when the mechanism that applies it is running and verified.

data.title: Apple Configurator (cfgutil)
data.notes: Installed on LAB 512 (macOS). The Apple Hardware Bridge uses only operations validated on that host.

data.title: EmDash is the Powerfarm platform
data.context: Recovery, graph and knowledge needed a home.
data.decision: Build everything as EmDash content, relations, plugin storage and a native plugin.
data.alternatives: Separate ARCC application; external graph database.
data.consequences: One installation, one database, one permission model.

data.title: Approval is publication
data.context: Destructive operations need a human decision bound to an exact version.
data.decision: A recovery operation is approved by publishing it; the job records the published revision.
data.consequences: EmDash revisions are the audit of what was approved; MCP and plugins cannot publish operations.

data.title: Link fields for operational records
data.context: Plugin and MCP writes cannot set relation-bound references.
data.decision: Operations, events and evidence link by business key; knowledge relationships use native relations.
data.alternatives: Core patch exposing reference writes to plugins.
data.consequences: Links validated on save; graph shows both kinds.

data.title: Journal in plugin storage, events as projection
data.decision: Hash-chained journal in EmDash plugin storage, projected to Events through an outbox.
data.alternatives: Events content as the only record.
data.consequences: Projection failures are retried and visible; audit-degraded blocks trust.

data.title: Mac DFU stays manual
data.context: No automated Apple-silicon DFU route has been validated.
data.decision: Mac revive/restore are Finder procedures on a second Mac with macOS 14+; outcomes recorded in EmDash.
data.consequences: The bridge never touches a Mac.

data.title: SQLite for Mission 001
data.context: Single process on LAB 512; EmDash search uses FTS5 on SQLite.
data.consequences: Simple backup; revisit if multiple processes are needed. EmDash FTS is SQLite-only.

data.title: Private media files
data.decision: A small, isolated EmDash patch makes media files require authentication when EMDASH_PRIVATE_MEDIA=1.
data.consequences: Evidence is in EmDash media and not public.

data.title: Reference writes for trusted plugins (patch 0002)
data.context: Onboarding blueprints must create records linked by native relations; EmDash's plugin content.create drops references.
data.decision: Patch EmDash so in-process plugins may pass references to content.create, validated by EmDash's own create handler in the same transaction; sandboxed plugins are refused. Recovery records keep link fields (ADR-0003).
data.alternatives: Link fields for every new entity; asking a person to link every created record.
data.consequences: Native relations for entities; one more EmDash patch to carry on upgrades.

data.title: Entity status comes from evidence-backed controls
data.context: A 'secure' or 'active' flag anyone can set proves nothing.
data.decision: Lifecycle changes are publications checked against controls derived from attestations, relations, the identity registry and approved exceptions.
data.alternatives: Editable status fields; checklists outside EmDash.
data.consequences: Activation can be refused with a list of what is missing; nothing activates automatically.

data.title: Cloudflare holds the state; the lab Macs do the compute
data.context: The lab is less available than a cloud service, and computing in the cloud costs too much for device work.
data.decision: Run EmDash on Cloudflare (Workers, D1, R2, Cron Trigger) behind Cloudflare Access; keep device work and large files on the lab Macs, which pull jobs and report back through a disk outbox.
data.alternatives: EmDash on a VM in the lab (ADR-0006); compute in the cloud.
data.consequences: Nothing in the lab is reachable from the internet; a lab outage delays jobs but never loses what Powerfarm records. D1 is SQLite, so ADR-0006's search reasoning holds. Two locks: Access, then EmDash's own sign-in.

data.title: A thin MDM inside the Powerfarm plugin
data.context: Six devices were compromised and attacks continue; the fleet needs continuous management, and EmDash already provides routes, storage, content, cron and audit.
data.decision: Implement Apple's MDM protocol in the Powerfarm plugin: device messages verified against a Powerfarm device CA whose key stays on the lab Mac; profiles approved by publishing; findings as incidents; a posture score for Cloudflare Access. The enrolment grants no erase, lock or passcode rights.
data.alternatives: A commercial MDM; a separate MDM server.
data.consequences: One platform; a compromised Powerfarm cannot wipe or lock the fleet; pushes go through the lab Mac, so a lab outage delays commands.

data.title: Powerfarm Identity: principals, grants and federation on EmDash
data.context: Access to the institution must not depend on any one person's account, and authority must be explicit, scoped and auditable.
data.decision: Every principal (organisation, person, agent, service, device) is EmDash content with a permanent principal_id; sign-in identities are entries in the identifier registry; authority is published grants checked by one authorize() decision on every governed path; Powerfarm is the OIDC provider for Cloudflare Access; published institutional records are sealed.
data.alternatives: A separate identity platform or directory; roles as the only authority; Cloudflare or Apple as the identity root.
data.consequences: One identity model; suspension and revocation take effect at Powerfarm's gates at once; EmDash core administration stays governed by EmDash roles behind a stricter Access application.

data.title: Human approval boundary
data.statement: Only a person can approve a recovery operation; AI clients draft only.

data.title: Simulations never count
data.statement: No simulated or dry-run result satisfies a recovery milestone.

data.title: Fail-closed verification
data.statement: Identity must match exactly; missing data fails.

data.title: Media-backed evidence
data.statement: Evidence is stored in EmDash media with a server-computed digest.

data.title: Graph access control
data.statement: The graph never reveals drafts, fields or identifiers a caller may not see.

data.title: One active job per device
data.statement: No two jobs act on one device at once; unknown outcomes block retries.

data.title: Identifiers unique across types
data.statement: An identifier (VAT, LEI, domain …) identifies one record of any type; duplicates are refused, also under concurrency.

data.title: No automatic activation
data.statement: Creating or registering a record never activates it, grants authority, signs an agreement or provisions anything.

data.result_summary: Recorded at release time; see Releases.

data.title: Powerfarm EmDash Platform 1.1.0
data.notes: Mission 001 corrections: simulation semantics, fail-closed verification, journal and outbox, media evidence, graph access control, native admin integration.

data.title: Powerfarm EmDash Platform 1.2.0
data.notes: Entities (clients, products, services, service instances, contracts), identity registry as content, classification and evidence-backed lifecycle controls, onboarding blueprints run as work items. EmDash patch 0002 (plugin reference writes).

data.title: Powerfarm EmDash Platform 1.2.2
data.notes: Deployment on Cloudflare (Workers, D1, R2, Access) with the lab Macs as pull workers; D1-safe reads; bridge outbox for lab outages; lifecycle integrity (active records keep their controls, registered records leave by retirement, merges wait for relinking). ADR-0010.

data.title: Powerfarm EmDash Platform 1.3.0
data.notes: Powerfarm Identity, first part: a thin MDM in the plugin (check-in and commands, device signatures against the Powerfarm device CA, approved profiles, vigilance and incidents, Cloudflare Access posture score, pushes and enrolment through the lab Mac). ADR-0011.

data.title: Powerfarm EmDash Platform 1.4.0
data.notes: Powerfarm Identity: organisations, people and agents as principals with permanent ids; grants and policies; the authorize() boundary; suspension; record seals; Access assertion check and identity/whoami; OIDC provider for Cloudflare Access; release gate; Access log feed. ADR-0012.

data.title: Powerfarm EmDash Platform
data.summary: EmDash as Powerfarm's institutional platform: graph, Mission 001 recovery, engineering records.

data.title: Trusted host bootstrap (LAB 512)
data.preconditions: Done before EmDash exists on LAB 512. Recorded afterwards with recordOnly.
data.required_tools: LAB 512's own macOS Recovery; if DFU is needed, A second, trusted Mac running macOS 14 or later, connected directly with a USB-C data cable that supports data to the target's DFU port. LAB 001 (Catalina, Intel) cannot act as the DFU host, and neither can the Linux VM. Or Apple-authorised service.
data.physical_steps:
1. Try macOS Recovery on LAB 512: shut down, hold the power button until 'Loading startup options', choose Options, then erase and reinstall macOS.
2. Only if that is impossible: DFU revive or restore from the second Mac's Finder.
3. Set up with a new administrator account and Powerfarm's own Apple Account. Do not migrate data, profiles or apps.
data.expected_results: LAB 512 boots a clean macOS, FileVault on, no unknown profiles, Activation Lock tied to Powerfarm's account.
data.failure_instructions: If Recovery and DFU both fail, stop and use Apple-authorised service.

children.text: EmDash cannot vouch for the machine it runs on, so LAB 512 is recovered independently and the method and result are recorded once EmDash is available.

data.title: iPhone inventory
data.preconditions: Device connected to the bridge host, unlocked, host trusted.
data.required_tools: Apple Configurator (cfgutil) on the bridge host, validated for inventory.
data.physical_steps: Connect the iPhone with a USB cable. Unlock it and tap Trust when asked.
data.expected_results: Serial number, ECID, model and iOS version reported.
data.failure_instructions: If the device does not appear, try another cable and port; check it is unlocked.

children.text: Read-only. Copy the reported serial number and ECID onto the asset yourself; the platform never writes identity automatically.

data.title: Mac inventory (manual)
data.preconditions: Mac powered on, or in DFU mode on the DFU host if its ECID is wanted.
data.required_tools: About This Mac / System Information; Apple Configurator on the DFU host for the ECID.
data.physical_steps: Open Apple menu → System Settings → General → About and note the serial number. Optionally read the ECID from Apple Configurator on the DFU host.
data.expected_results: Serial number recorded; ECID recorded if DFU is used.
data.failure_instructions: If the Mac will not boot, record the serial from the underside or the original packaging and mark the source.

children.text: Complete the manual job with the observed values and attach a screenshot or report.

data.title: iPhone backup
data.preconditions: Device connected and unlocked. Enough space on the bridge host.
data.physical_steps: Keep the iPhone unlocked until the backup completes.
data.expected_results: A local backup and its manifest.
data.failure_instructions: If the backup fails, decide explicitly whether to waive it before any restore.

children.text: Preserve user data selectively. Do not restore settings, profiles or apps from an untrusted installation.

data.title: Manual data preservation
data.preconditions: Decide which user files are worth keeping.
data.required_tools: External disk or the trusted host.
data.physical_steps: Copy only user documents you need. Do not copy system settings, profiles, certificates or applications.
data.expected_results: A manifest of what was kept, with hashes.
data.failure_instructions: If nothing is needed, record 'no user data' on the restore instead.

data.title: iPhone erase and restore
data.preconditions: Data-preservation decision recorded on the operation. Identity confirmed by inventory.
data.physical_steps: Connect the iPhone. If it does not appear, put it in recovery mode. Type the asset tag at the bridge when asked.
data.expected_results: Device erased with current iOS from Apple; setup assistant shown.
data.failure_instructions: If the restore stops part-way, do not retry. The job becomes needs_inspection; inspect the device and record what you see.

children.text: Destructive. One per device at a time.

data.title: Mac erase and reinstall from macOS Recovery
data.preconditions: Data-preservation decision recorded. Serial number recorded.
data.required_tools: The Mac's own macOS Recovery and a network connection.
data.physical_steps: Shut down. Hold the power button until 'Loading startup options'. Choose Options, open Disk Utility to erase, then Reinstall macOS.
data.expected_results: Clean macOS at the setup assistant.
data.failure_instructions: If Recovery cannot erase or reinstall, use P-MAC-REVIVE, then P-MAC-RESTORE.

children.text: Manual. Complete the job afterwards with the outcome and attach evidence.

data.title: Mac DFU revive (Finder)
data.preconditions: A second, trusted Mac running macOS 14 or later, connected directly with a USB-C data cable that supports data to the target's DFU port. LAB 001 (Catalina, Intel) cannot act as the DFU host, and neither can the Linux VM.
data.physical_steps: Put the target Mac into DFU mode and connect it to the DFU host. In Finder, select the Mac and choose Revive Mac.
data.expected_results: Firmware and recoveryOS reinstalled; data kept.

children.text: Manual Finder procedure. No automated route has been validated.

data.title: Mac DFU erase and restore (Finder)
data.preconditions: A second, trusted Mac running macOS 14 or later, connected directly with a USB-C data cable that supports data to the target's DFU port. LAB 001 (Catalina, Intel) cannot act as the DFU host, and neither can the Linux VM. Data-preservation decision recorded.
data.physical_steps: Put the target Mac into DFU mode and connect it to the DFU host. In Finder, select the Mac, choose Restore Mac and confirm erasure.
data.expected_results: Mac erased; latest firmware and macOS installed.
data.failure_instructions: If the restore fails part-way, record it; inspect before trying again.

data.title: iPhone verification
data.preconditions: Restore completed. Asset has serial, ECID and an OS policy recorded.
data.physical_steps: Connect the restored iPhone to the bridge host.
data.expected_results: Serial and ECID match exactly; iOS meets the policy.
data.failure_instructions: Any mismatch blocks the device. Investigate before continuing.

data.title: Mac verification (manual)
data.preconditions: Restore completed. Serial and OS policy recorded.
data.physical_steps: Read the serial number and macOS version and build, and enter them when completing the job.
data.expected_results: Serial matches exactly; macOS meets the policy.

data.title: Account and security baseline
data.required_tools: The device and Powerfarm's own Apple Account.
data.physical_steps: Sign in with Powerfarm's Apple Account; turn on two-factor authentication and Find My; confirm Activation Lock belongs to that account; check there is no device-management enrolment or profile you do not recognise; set a passcode or FileVault.
data.expected_results: One attestation each for account security, Activation Lock and management enrolment, recorded after the latest restore.
data.failure_instructions: If the device is enrolled in management you do not recognise, stop: do not remove ownership information; contact the organisation that owns the enrolment or Apple.

children.text: Record each check as an Evidence attestation.

data.title: Inspect after an interrupted operation
data.physical_steps: Look at the device without starting anything: setup screen, recovery mode, old system, or unresponsive?
data.expected_results: A written finding on the job, then a fresh inventory.
data.failure_instructions: If the device is unresponsive, try recovery mode or DFU only after recording the finding.

children.text: Guidance only; cannot be approved as an operation.

data.title: Mission 001 — Neutralization and trusted recovery
data.objective: Establish a trusted recovery path, stop relying on untrusted installations, rebuild LAB 512, LAB 8GB, LAB 256, iPhone 13 RED, iPhone 14 PURPLE and iPhone 15 BLACK, and verify them.
data.acceptance: All six recovery targets are 'trusted': real restore, exact identity verification after it, security attestations after it, intact audit journal, and an administrator's trust sign-off.

children.text: LAB 001 is the communications terminal and is not a recovery target.
LAB 512 is recovered first and independently, then hosts EmDash (in an Ubuntu VM) and the Apple Hardware Bridge (on macOS).
iPhones are handled by the bridge; Macs by documented manual procedures. Every destructive step is a recovery operation that a person approves by publishing it.

data.title: Client onboarding
data.description: When a client registration is approved: owner, identity, classification and access reviews, product links, a draft agreement for review, a maintenance plan.

steps.title: Confirm the accountable owner for {{subject.title}}
steps.description: Set the client's Accountable owner in the editor and publish.

steps.title: Verify the identity of {{subject.title}}
steps.description: Check each identifier with its issuer. Record an identity_verified attestation (Evidence, subject {{subject.ref}}) naming the identifier; attach the issuer's record if you have it.

steps.title: Review the classification of {{subject.title}} ({{subject.classification}})
steps.description: Confirm the classification fits the information held. Record a classification_reviewed attestation.

steps.title: Review who may access {{subject.title}}'s records
steps.description: Confidential and restricted clients need an administrator's access_reviewed attestation before activation.

steps.title: Link the products and shared services {{subject.title}} uses
steps.description: Select existing Products on the client and publish. Do not register a second copy of a service that is already in the catalogue.

steps.title: Review the draft agreement for {{subject.title}}
steps.description: Open the draft contract this run created. Approve when its terms are ready to negotiate. Approving does not sign it: signing is a contract_signed attestation with the signed copy.

steps.title: Set the review cadence for {{subject.title}} and record a maintenance plan
Onboarding work for {{subject.title}} is in place

data.failure_procedure: Open Powerfarm → Automation, read the failed step, fix the cause, then mark the step resolved or cancel the run. Never re-register the client to re-run onboarding.
